proposedOverrides.name: Hopewell Culture
proposedOverrides.summary: Hopewell names a network of Indigenous communities and ceremonial traditions, rather than one kingdom.

batchIdentityNotes.assessment: Wari/Huari same polity; decoded broad Peruvian extent supports identity but is not a precision map of control. Imported 600 to 1279 span badly exceeds conventional 600 to 1000/1100 imperial phase. Narrative and periods use actual historical development and explicitly flag 1279. Root should retain dateBasis map_coverage; no geometry/date repair done.

Tiwanaku/Tiahuanaco same center; broad outline spans Titicaca and coastal regions, not proof of uniform territorial administration. Imported 600 to 1279 endpoint far later than city collapse. Marsh et al. 2023 current corrected article models rapid city collapse ~1010 to 1050; does not transpose this to all related settlements. Older UNESCO 11th/12th-century sequence deliberately not adopted.

Ceremonial center and wider cultural/religious sphere, not demonstrated unified empire. Decoded polygon includes Chavín de Huántar; cannot establish political boundary. 1000 BCE to 1 BCE map dates do not establish the temple’s main flourishing; focused recent studies use about 1100 to 400 BCE.

Southern Peru archaeological culture, variable local communities and stages. Extent generally supports coastal identity, not a unitary kingdom. Map endpoint 600 CE precedes typical late phase ending ~750 CE; period context extends accordingly. No single disappearance imposed.

Southern coastal cultural tradition. Imported 400 to 100 BCE slice is narrower than development and mortuary traditions. Paracas Necropolis/Wari Kayán has strong Topará associations and roughly 150 BCE to 200 CE dates; card explicitly distinguishes this from uniform Paracas culture. No duplicate polity inferred from textiles.

Norte Chico/Caral-Supe early complex societies in north-central Peruvian valleys. Imported polygon stretches to about 16.46° S, much farther south than core Supe/Pativilca/Fortaleza/Huaura valleys, and 4000 BCE start precedes monumental centers discussed. Broad outline cannot establish single state or precise culture boundary. Narrative flags both limitations.

MAJOR UNRESOLVED GEOMETRY ERROR: polygon ends near 92.10° W while actual Poverty Point is near 91.40° W, 32.64° N, east of imported shape. It extends across western Louisiana/Arkansas/Oklahoma region and misses the type site. Narrative follows label and explicitly warns. Imported 1500 to 1000 BCE is a rough slice of main 1700 to 1100 BCE occupation. 2025 gathering interpretation attributed and contrasted with residential model. No geometry correction done.

Interconnected eastern North American communities, especially Ohio ceremonial earthworks, not an empire or one ethnicity. Huge decoded footprint can only be schematic interaction sphere. Imported 100 BCE to 600 CE differs from commonly described 100 BCE to 500 CE main flourishing. Descendant Native communities continue.
